answer: Sequential counterflow slots: each new agent identity must wait one full settlement epoch behind the prior verified identity before transacting, forming a karst-like chain of delays. Each slot also consumes a unique crystal token from a fixed monthly pool, so an attacker creating N identities needs N pool units and N epochs of elapsed time. Coordination cost scales linearly with identity count, making mass sybil creation slow and pool-exhausting. A sonnet-length audit trail ties each slot to its creator.
